simple.meaning: נְפִיל (nᵉphîyl) is a Hebrew word meaning “properly, a feller , i.e. a bully or tyrant.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: נְפִיל (H5303) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Genesis 6:4, with occurrences in Genesis, Numbers.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נְפִיל (H5303) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in נְפִיל (H5303) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: נְפִיל (nᵉphîyl) / H5303 is traced through Genesis 6:4, Numbers 13:33 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H5303. Nephilim נְפִלִים noun masculine plural giants , according to ᵐ5 γίγαντες so ᵑ9 ᵑ6 ; הַנְּפִלִים Gen 6:4 (J), מִןהַֿנְּפִלִים עֲנָק בְּנֵי הַנְּפִילִים Num 13:33 (JE); ᵐ5 omit וגו ׳בְּנֵי , and so Di; these words perhaps doublet, but already in ⅏ , also ᵑ9 (etymology dubious; compare Aramaic נְפִילָא נִיפְלָא, Orion ; conjectures see in Thes Di on the passage ; Tu Kn Len Or. i. 344, Eng. Tr. 345 f. ; Che Hebraica. iii (1887), 175, 176 ; all very precarious).
